report: Regelrechte Artikulationsverhältnisse femorotibial und femoropatellar. Homogenes Knochenmarksignal, kein Bone Bruise / Knochenödem. Femorotibial homogener Knorpelbesatz im medialen und lateralen Kompartiment, keine tiefgreifende Chondropathie-Areale. Auch retropatellar homogener Knorpelüberzug. Unauffällige Signalgebung von Innenmeniskus und Außenmeniskus, keine fassbare Rissbildung. Kreuzbänder intakt. Medialer und lateraler Kollateralbandapparat ohne Auffälligkeiten. Quadriceps- und Patellarsehne intakt und ohne tendinopathische Signalveränderungen. Minimal akzentuierte Gelenkflüssigkeit, kein ausgeprägter Gelenkerguss. Plica mediopatellaris (Typ C n. Sakakibara). Ca. 8 mm durchmessende, nicht erhabene, T2w hyperintense kutane Läsion medialseitig knapp oberhalb des femorotibialen Gelenkspalts.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Transformación quística parcial del tercio proximal del LCA. LCP y ligamentos colaterales dentro de límites
normales.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial que contacta la superficie
articular inferior sugieran una rotura.
Rotura del cuerno anterior, cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco lateral con mínima extrusión. Esto se
asocia a edema las partes blandas regionales.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral
medial. Úlceras condrales espesor parcial de la región central del platillo tibial lateral. Condropatía
superficial del resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total de distribución difusa de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con discreta sinovitis. No hay quistes poplíteos.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de
límites normales.
Impresión:
Signos de una rotura del menisco medial, no desplazada.
Rotura compleja del cuerno anterior, cuerpo y cuerno posterior del menisco lateral con mínima extrusión y
edema de las partes blandas regionales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial y del
platillo tibial lateral.
Condropatía superficial del resto de los compartimentos femorotibiales.
Condropatía lesiones grado 2 y 3 de la rótula.
Leve derrame articular con discreta sinovitis difusa.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain right knee, initial encounter.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Horizontal tear of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus which is partially extruded.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade cartilage defects and irregularity of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	High-grade cartilage defects of the right medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.
2.	Horizontal tear of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus.
3.	Small right knee joint effusion.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. Large complex popliteal cyst measuring up to 65 mm with an 11 mm osseous body in the superior aspect of the cyst. Sliver of free fluid along the inferior margin of the popliteal cyst suggesting minimal recent partial rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Moderate degenerative change.
Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal horizontal oblique component of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with inferior surfacing. Fraying and blunting of the meniscal free edge.
Mild thickening of the proximal MCL compatible with remote injury.
Diffuse low grade partial-thickness chondral loss. Marginal osteophytosis.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Severe degenerative change with full-thickness chondral loss of the weightbearing and posterior portion of the compartment, with subchondral reactive marrow change. Marginal osteophytosis.
Complex degenerative multidirectional tear of the posterior horn extending into the body with significant maceration and substance loss of the body and anterior and posterior horn with minimal residual meniscal substance. There is some extrusion of the body of the lateral meniscus.
Thickened popliteus insertion with intrasubstance signal compatible with moderate tendinosis
Mildly thickened lateral collateral ligament proper which could reflect the sequela of a remote injury. Mild distal biceps tendinosis.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Degenerative changes of the anterior cruciate ligament which remains intact. The PCL is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild chondropathy. Small marginal osteophytes. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Mild edema at the suprapatellar fat pad.
Scarring at that the Hoffa's fat pad which could reflect the previous surgery-for clinical correlation.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
The intra-articular body is seen at the suprapatellar joint recess on the previous MRI is no longer present.

CONCLUSION:
1.Interval worsening of the severe osteoarthritis of the lateral compartment. Complex degenerative tearing and extensive maceration the lateral meniscus.
2.Moderate degenerative change of the medial compartment. Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus.
3.Mild degenerative change of the patellofemoral compartment.
4.Large complex popliteal cyst with an osseous body.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multisequence multiplanar MRI of the left knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Meniscus injury?

COMPARISON:  Radiographs of bilateral knees [Date].

FINDINGS:
There is a 5 mm intermediate signal particle along the medial aspect of the medial femoral condyle, deep to the medial collateral ligament. This was present as a small mineralized focus on the prior radiographs from <[Month]> <[YEAR]>, stable in size. No adjacent soft tissue or bone marrow edema.

The cruciate and collateral ligaments are intact. Minimal thickening of the medial collateral ligament proximally is suggestive of remote low-grade injury/sprain. Posterolateral corner supporting structures of the knee are intact.

There is an oblique radial/parrot beak tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. No displaced flap fragment. No parameniscal cyst. Borderline extrusion of the medial meniscus mid body.

The lateral meniscus is intact.

There is a full-thickness chondral defect over the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle, measuring approximately 1.6 x 1.0 cm (AP x ML). No subchondral marrow edema or fracture. Articular cartilage is otherwise well-maintained in the lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartments.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

Moderate joint effusion. No synovitis. Small Baker's cyst, without evidence of cystic compression/rupture.


INTERPRETATION:
 Oblique radial tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
Full-thickness chondral defect over the central weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle without subchondral marrow edema.
